findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category is not set or matches no category
findings.body: The category lookup does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i`. If no `embed_category` row exists in site_settings, or its value matches no category name (the common case, since the default was ''), the result set is empty. `[0]` then returns nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The migration aborts on most installs and blocks deploys. The fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` on line 14 is never reached. The same nil-indexing problem applies on line 15 if `uncategorized_category_id` was never persisted to site_settings.

findings.title: Unescaped, unnormalized host values interpolated into INSERT
findings.body:
Each legacy host string is interpolated directly into SQL as `'#{h}'` without quoting. A value containing a quote breaks the migration and is a SQL-injection vector.

The values are also inserted without the model's normalization. Strings split on "\n" keep trailing "\r" or whitespace, and the old setting allowed `http://` prefixes, which the old lookup stripped. Rows like `http://example.com` or `example.com\r` never match `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, so previously working embeds silently stop working after upgrade.

Fix: strip whitespace and the scheme/path from each value, skip blanks, and use `connection.quote` for the insert.

findings.title: Irreversible data deletion inside a `change` migration
findings.body: The migration deletes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings in `change`. On rollback, `create_table` is reversed (the table is dropped) but the deleted settings are not restored. Rolling back permanently loses the embedding configuration. Use explicit `up`/`down` methods, or raise `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration` in `down`.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on nil host
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally. If host is nil, for example when the request params omit `embeddable_host[host]`, this raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if host.present?`, or use non-mutating `sub` on `host.to_s`.

findings.title: Hosts with ports or uppercase referers never match
findings.body: Matching is done with `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, but the query value is not lowercased, so a referer with uppercase letters in its hostname is rejected. In addition, the validation explicitly allows a `:port` suffix, and the before_validation keeps it. `uri.host` never includes the port, so a stored `example.com:8080` can never match. Lowercase the input, and either strip ports on save or compare against host plus port.

findings.title: Host validation rejects valid hostnames
findings.body: The regex requires a final label matching `\.[a-z]{2,5}`. This rejects valid hosts such as `localhost` and TLDs longer than 5 characters (e.g. `.museum`, `.technology`, `.photography`). Admins cannot add these hosts through the new UI, even though the migration can insert such values unvalidated.

findings.title: Update/destroy of a missing id raises NoMethodError
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown or already-deleted id. The next call (`host.host=` in save_host, or `host.destroy`) then raises a 500. Use `find` or `find_by!` so the request returns a proper 404.

findings.title: `_ids` hydration crashes on null and keeps unresolved ids as undefined
findings.body:
Any key ending in `_ids` is assumed to be an array. If the server sends `foo_ids: null`, `obj[k].map` throws and the whole find fails.

Also, `hydrated || []` is dead code because `map` always returns an array. Ids that are not found in the side-loaded collection become `undefined` entries, and the original ids are deleted. Guard against non-arrays and filter out unresolved entries (or keep the ids).

findings.title: find embedded test requests fruit 2 but stub always returns fruit 1
findings.body: The test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)`, but the pretender handler for `/fruits/:id` always returns `fruits[0]` (apple, `color_ids [1,2]`). The assertions on two colors with ids 1 and 2 only pass because of that stub. Fruit 2 (banana) has a single color, id 3. The test is misleading and does not check that the requested record is the one hydrated.

findings.title: Spec name no longer matches behavior under test
findings.body: The spec "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false. `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks embeddable hosts at all, and `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in the nested context has no effect on the result. The test name describes behavior that does not exist and gives false coverage.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents swapped
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, and the new `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. It works because all fabricators are loaded, but the contents of the two files are swapped and will confuse future maintainers. Swap them back.

findings.title: String replace only converts the first underscore
findings.body: `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first occurrence. Any admin model type with more than one underscore (e.g. `site_customization_foo`) will not match ADMIN_MODELS and will be routed to the non-admin path. Use `replace(/_/g, '-')` or `Ember.String.dasherize`.
